Deep Cleaning Checklist

A deep clean goes after the build-up a weekly tidy never touches — the greasy extractor filter, the limescale in the kettle, the dust on top of the doorframes. This checklist works through the whole home so nothing gets skipped in the once- or twice-a-year reset. Tackle it over a weekend, or split it across a few evenings. See more cleaning and chore checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Deep Cleaning Checklist · 20 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Dust from the top down: light fixtures, ceiling corners, and the tops of doorframes and wardrobes

    Dust falls, so always start high and finish at the floor.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Wash walls, switch plates, and skirting boards with a damp microfiber cloth
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Clean windows inside and out, including the tracks and sills

    A cotton bud lifts the grime packed into the corners of the tracks.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Launder the curtains and wipe down blinds slat by slat
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Descale the kettle and coffee machine with a vinegar or citric-acid solution
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Degrease the extractor hood and soak or replace its filter

    Metal filters can go through a hot dishwasher cycle.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Deep-clean the oven: remove the racks to soak, and scrub the interior glass
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Pull out the fridge, defrost the freezer, and wipe the coils and door seals
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Empty and wipe every kitchen cupboard, checking food dates while you're in there
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Run an empty hot cycle with cleaner in the washing machine and dishwasher

    Wipe the rubber door seal and clear the dishwasher filter.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Scrub the grout and re-caulk any mouldy sealant around the bath and sink
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Descale the showerhead by soaking it in vinegar overnight
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Disinfect and descale the toilet, including the base and behind the bowl
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Vacuum and flip the mattresses, and wash mattress protectors and pillows
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Wash or dry-clean duvets, and vacuum the divan or bed base
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Move furniture to vacuum underneath, then shampoo carpets or mop hard floors
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Wipe down radiators and vacuum the dust from between the fins
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Disinfect high-touch spots: light switches, door handles, and remote controls
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Vacuum upholstered sofas and chairs, including under the cushions
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Empty, wash, and disinfect every bin, including the kitchen caddy

Frequently asked questions

How often should I deep clean my house? expand_more

Most homes need a full deep clean once or twice a year — often in spring and before winter — on top of your weekly routine. High-traffic spots like the kitchen and bathroom benefit from a deeper monthly go at the oven, extractor filter, and grout.

What's the difference between deep cleaning and regular cleaning? expand_more

Regular cleaning keeps surfaces tidy week to week — wiping counters, vacuuming, and cleaning the toilet. Deep cleaning goes after the built-up grime those routines skip: inside the oven, behind the fridge, limescale in the kettle, grout, mattresses, and the tops of doorframes.

What order should I deep clean a room in? expand_more

Work top to bottom and dry to wet. Dust high surfaces first so falling debris lands on floors you haven't done yet, tackle greasy and wet jobs like the oven and bathroom in the middle, and finish by vacuuming and mopping the floor last so you don't tread dirt back over clean areas.
